_comment: Recommended judge settings per vision model. Choosing a model in Settings fills these in (the first preset that fits both the backend in use and the model name wins; a preset without 'backends' fits any). 'prompt_token_budget' is an absolute cap on the judge prompt: long-context accuracy starts dropping around 10-20% of a model's window and the middle of a long prompt is recalled worst, so prompts are kept short and the key parts sit at the start and end.

presets.label: Gemma 4 26B-A4B (DeepInfra), best judge tested
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): the only model whose every good-image score stayed above every flawed one (review margin +2.6, confirm +8.2); 11 s a call, $0.32 per 1000 calls. It doesn't reason by default; reasoning_effort low made it 10x slower and 5x dearer for no gain, and 768 px images didn't help. Writes adult prompts. It scores high, so the threshold is 80. In 5 real rendered jobs (2026-10-04) its final images tied for best with an outside referee (55.1 of 100), but its own scores didn't track the referee's (correlation -0.03) and at 80 it passed only 2 of 5 jobs, running ~6 rounds on average.

presets.label: Gemma 4 31B turbo (DeepInfra)
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): as accurate as the 26B (confirm margin +3.9) but about twice as slow (20 s a call), $0.31 per 1000 calls. Leave reasoning off (low: 108 s a call). Writes adult prompts. Threshold 79. Best in 5 real rendered jobs (2026-10-04): best final image on 4 of 5 references by an outside referee (55.2 of 100), passed 3 of 5 at 79 in ~4 rounds, 18 min and $0.018 a job, and its own scores tracked the referee's (correlation 0.74).

presets.label: DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision (DeepInfra), fastest
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): with reasoning_effort none: 3 s a call, $0.40 per 1000 calls, every labelled pair right; good and flawed scores overlap by ~1-2 points, so a borderline image can pass. With reasoning on it was 15x slower, 10x dearer and less consistent. Writes adult prompts (unlike DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Threshold 69. In 5 real rendered jobs (2026-10-04): third (referee 52.1), fastest jobs (11 min), $0.030 a job, passed 4 of 5.

presets.label: MiMo V2.6 Flash (DeepInfra), cheapest
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): with reasoning_effort none: 3.6 s a call, $0.13 per 1000 calls; ranks every labelled pair right but names the flaw in 83% of looks (others 100%). Writes adult prompts. Threshold 71. Takes at most 4 images a request (the backend leaves the rest out). In 5 real rendered jobs (2026-10-04): referee 44.7 of 100, well behind the Gemmas.

presets.label: Qwen3.8 27B (DeepInfra)
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): with reasoning_effort none: 12 s a call, $1.37 per 1000 calls, as accurate as with reasoning (60 s, $6.50 per 1000). Its scores run low and good and flawed images overlap by ~3-8 points. Writes adult prompts. Threshold 66. In 5 real rendered jobs (2026-10-04): last by the referee (43.0 of 100) and the dearest ($0.056 a job).

presets.label: MiniMax M3 (DeepInfra)
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): with reasoning_effort none: 15 s a call, $0.72 per 1000 calls; accurate rankings but scores run low (good images ~66). Writes adult prompts. Threshold 62.

presets.label: GLM 5.3 Flash (DeepInfra)
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): 30 s a call, $0.34 per 1000 calls, and often 'model busy' (429). Ranks pairs right but one look at an image can move 8 points. Writes adult prompts. Threshold 62.

presets.label: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite (DeepInfra)
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): 13 s a call but $5.37 per 1000 calls (17x Gemma 4 26B) for no better judging. Writes adult prompts. Threshold 73.

presets.label: Seed 2.0 mini (DeepInfra), not recommended
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): no JSON-schema support (answers in plain JSON mode), good and flawed images overlap by 10-14 points; 16 s a call with reasoning_effort none. Threshold 54 if used.

presets.label: Llama 4 Scout (DeepInfra), not recommended
presets.notes: Measured 2026-10-03 on eval/judge_set.json (11 images x 5 looks, the loop's own judge call): ranked 64-82% of labelled pairs right and scored a flawed image above good ones by up to 26 points. Fast (12 s) and cheap, but not a usable judge.

presets.label: DeepSeek V4 Flash (DeepInfra)
presets.notes: Hosted vision model: nothing to load locally, several calls can run at once, and a judged round costs a fraction of a cent. It reasons before answering, so leave room for the answer (max_tokens 8192). Temperature 0 keeps the same image's score stable between looks, which is what makes the pass threshold mean anything. Note: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash refuses adult (NSFW) prompts; DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp doesn't.

presets.label: Qwen3-VL (thinking)
presets.notes: Thinks before answering: 100-270 s per judge call in tests, and at temperature 0 it loops until num_predict. Prefer an -instruct tag.

presets.label: Qwen3-VL instruct
presets.notes: Temperature 0: judging the same image twice moved the score by 0.3-0.5 points, against 8-10 points at 0.7, at the same speed (measured with python -m ouroboros eval). A stable score is what makes the threshold mean something.

presets.label: Qwen2.5-VL
presets.notes: Temperature 0: judging the same image twice moved the score by 0.3-0.5 points, against 8-10 points at 0.7, at the same speed (measured with python -m ouroboros eval). A stable score is what makes the threshold mean something.

presets.label: Llama 3.2 Vision
presets.notes: One image per message, so the reference and candidates go as one grid (up to 1120 px). Older uploads such as Drews54/llama3.2-vision-abliterated don't load in Ollama 0.34+.

presets.label: Gemma 3
presets.notes: Several images per message; Google's recommended sampling.

presets.label: OpenAI
presets.notes: Large window; the budget still keeps prompts short and cheap.

presets.label: DeepInfra hosted model
presets.notes: Generic settings for a hosted vision model. Check the model's page for its context window and whether it reasons before answering (which needs a larger max_tokens).
